node_modules/@base-ui/react/docs/react/components/tooltip.md (parts table, data attributes, CSS vars, arrow/animation examples, accessibility notes)
semanticDifferences: Root.disabled replaces isDisabled and blocks opening, but Base UI never disables the trigger element itself (it only emits data-trigger-disabled) — the native disabled attribute is applied by our TooltipTrigger via an internal context that stands in for React Aria's ButtonContext propagation.

Trigger delay/closeDelay live on Trigger, not Root, so Tooltip forwards them to the trigger element it renders. Base UI's default delay is 600ms; the payload's 300ms default is passed explicitly, so the default is unchanged.

React Aria's tooltip warmup (module-global in react-stately: a recently shown tooltip makes the next hover open instantly for max(500ms, closeDelay) and opening one tooltip closes the others) has no Base UI equivalent outside Tooltip.Provider delay groups, so it is ported verbatim into module scope here.

Positioning is Portal > Positioner > Popup with side/align/sideOffset/alignOffset instead of placement/offset/crossOffset; React Aria's placement strings are mapped (start/end stay logical => inline-start/inline-end).

Animation is attribute driven: data-starting-style exists for a single frame and data-ending-style for the whole exit phase, so the enter classes hang off data-open (see stateSelectorChanges). Base UI also sets data-instant, which React Aria had no analogue for; no instant-specific classes were added because Tailwind orders data-open:* after data-instant:* at equal specificity (verified with a compiled probe), so an instant override would not win.

The Base UI Tooltip emits no ARIA role/description wiring at all (verified across tooltip/**/*.mjs): role="tooltip", the popup id and the trigger's aria-describedby are restored here exactly as React Aria emitted them.

React Aria positioned the arrow on both axes inline (`top|bottom|left|right: 100%` plus a translate-centred cross axis); Base UI only sets the cross axis, so the side-facing edge is supplied as a class on Tooltip.Arrow (measured pixel-identical afterwards).
arrowBoundaryOffset defaults to 0 in React Aria and 5 in Base UI, so arrowPadding is passed as `arrowBoundaryOffset ?? 0` to keep the arrow's clamping identical.

stateSelectorChanges.reason: React Aria kept data-entering (and the classes) until the enter animation finished (react-aria useEnterAnimation awaits element.getAnimations()). Base UI's data-starting-style exists for a single frame, which would cancel the one-shot animate-in keyframes; data-open is present for the whole open phase, so the enter animation plays exactly as before (verified: computed animation-name 'enter' and a full 150ms run).

Base UI emits data-side (not data-placement) on the Positioner, Popup and Arrow; the variant prefix was rewritten to the attribute Base UI actually renders (verified in the browser: data-side is present and the slide classes resolve).

evidence.notes: node node_modules/typescript5/bin/tsc -p registry/untitledui/tsconfig.json — clean for this file (sibling units still report their own in-flight errors, e.g. buttons/button.tsx useRef); node node_modules/typescript5/bin/tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json (app project, @types/node present) — clean for this file, which is why the warmup timer uses window.setTimeout/window.clearTimeout instead of a ReturnType-typed handle. Runtime verification (throwaway Vite harness in .smoke-tooltip, deleted afterwards; only this component imported): focus opens with role="tooltip" + id, data-open/data-side/data-align, animation-name 'enter', trigger gets data-popup-open + aria-describedby matching the popup id; Escape closes; hover after a close opens within 200ms (React Aria warmup preserved) while a cold hover still waits the full 300ms; disabled Tooltip renders a disabled trigger and never opens; a raw child element (no TooltipTrigger wrapper) registers as the trigger; controlled isOpen toggles and unlinks aria-describedby on close; exit sets data-ending-style and runs animation-name 'exit' before unmounting. Geometry was compared against the pre-migration file from HEAD rendered side by side with identical props: box size/padding/radius/background/z-index identical for all six placements, align offsets identical (-12/+12), and the arrow rect identical to the pixel (e.g. side=top: arrow at the box's bottom edge, 41px from its left edge, rotate 0deg; side=bottom: rotate 180deg at the top edge; side=left/right: rotate -90/90deg). Two recorded compat gaps neither of which blocks the migration: `trigger="focus"` can no longer suppress hover-open, and `isEntering`/`isExiting` are accepted but inert — both are unused across the registry. One environment-sensitive observation for the gates: Base UI waits for the exit animation to finish before unmounting (React Aria could bail out early and unmount immediately when its getAnimations() race saw no pending animation), so in a throttled/hidden tab the popup can linger a few hundred ms after close; in gate-like timing (single 260ms sleep, no DOM polling) both implementations unmount well inside the window. Also note .design-compiler/base-ui-migration/docs/tooltip.json is still absent from disk — the scout delivered it inline and only the lead may persist it.
